scenes.vo: This is OneBar. Ask about the weather on your route, and get one checked answer that fits in a single text.

visual.tagline: One bar of signal. One *checked* reply.

scenes.vo: You're up on a ridge with one bar of signal. Your weather app won't load, and the clouds are building.
You could ask a chatbot, but it might make up a number. Up here, a made-up storm time can hurt you.

lines: A chatbot can make up a number.
Up here, that's a *storm you didn't see*.

scenes.vo: OneBar splits the work. Code reads the forecast for your exact spot, a small model writes the reply, and a checker makes sure every number in it is real.
scenes.say: One Bar splits the work. Code reads the forecast for your exact spot, a small model writes the reply, and a checker makes sure every number in it is real.

actions.text: Ask about the weather on your route

scenes.vo: I'm near Zermatt, so I type storm before three and hit send. One short reply comes back, already checked.
Hover any number in it, and a line runs back to the forecast hour it came from. The model didn't guess any of them.
This one's a recorded question from our test set. Flip to the untuned base model, and its draft runs to two hundred and forty-one characters. That's too long for one text, so it never goes out.

actions.text: Or watch a recorded example, no place needed

scenes.vo: That's why OneBar runs its own model, an open Qwen fine-tuned on Tinker. On four hundred and fourteen questions at places it never saw, it passed the check first time ninety-eight percent of the time. The base model got just under fifty-seven.
scenes.say: That's why One Bar runs its own model, an open Kwen, fine-tuned on Tinker. On four hundred and fourteen questions at places it never saw, it passed the check first time ninety-eight percent of the time. The base model got just under fifty-seven.

actions.text: Does the tuned model beat the base model?

scenes.vo: If you're heading out alone, text trip with your return time and a contact. Miss your time without texting out, and your contact gets an email. Temporal keeps that timer running, even if the worker crashes.
